correctness.rationale: Exchangeability gives one diagonal and one off-diagonal covariance entry; the almost-sure unit-sum constraint fixes the off-diagonal entry exactly. The aggregate-gradient covariance is then a direct matrix pushforward and equals the centered task scatter. The sharp variance maximum follows from the simplex inequality between each coordinate and its square, with equality forcing a one-hot vector. The embedded verifier checks the identities on exact finite exchangeable laws.

value.rationale: The defining scientific justification for RLW emphasizes the benefit of extra stochasticity, yet the geometry of that noise determines what local directions it can actually explore. The theorem shows that all exchangeable RLW laws share one exact anisotropic support—the task-disagreement span—and that their distribution choice changes only covariance amplitude. It also identifies the source's one-task-at-a-time option as the unique maximum-noise endpoint and gives a pairwise disagreement energy formula, directly sharpening the method's escape-and-regularization interpretation.
